note: Ordered fix rules for `modaccel port -Fix`. `match` is a regex tested against each javac error's message + symbol + file. `apply.find` / `apply.replace` is a .NET regex replace in the affected source (named groups survive as ${name}); `apply.literal` is a plain string replace; `apply.ensureImports` adds an import only when the file lacks it. `scope` is `log` (only the files that error was reported in) or `repo` (every .java in the repo, for a family whose remaining call sites javac has not reached yet). `when` is an optional regex the candidate file's own text must match. `verified` names the repo, the count and the log a build actually proved it on; null means reasoned, not measured.

rules.match: incompatible types: Optional<(Boolean|Integer|Long|Float|Double|String|CompoundTag|ListTag)> cannot be converted|getList in class CompoundTag cannot be applied|no suitable method found for getList
rules.note: Every getter rule carries the same match: the whole Optional family, not one type. javac stops after the first wave, so a log that shows only Optional<Integer> still proves the target API and the sweep must cover the Boolean/Long/String sites it has not reached. The key group is a string literal, an ALL_CAPS constant or a single lowercase identifier (a ListTag index); the lookahead leaves a call that is already consumed as an Optional alone.
rules.verified: Traveler's Backpack 1.21.4->1.21.5: 39 sites in one round; the copy went 100 -> 6 reported errors, and with only the six removed-class imports hand-cleared javac reported 64 errors, none of them getter-family (bench/fix-test/tb, .runs/logs/port-fix-20261022-205549.log)

rules.match: getOrCreateTagBuilder
rules.note: Block and item providers hold registry values, so their builder is valueLookupBuilder(TagKey) -> ProvidedTagBuilder<T, T>. The fluent chain afterwards (add/addTag/setReplace/forceAddTag) is unchanged.

rules.note: A plain FabricTagProvider<T> (biomes) and an entity-type provider take builder(TagKey) -> ProvidedTagBuilder<RegistryKey<T>, T>. The entity-type one must use this form because it adds registry keys, not values.

rules.match: symbol:   method add\(Identifier\)|no suitable method found for add\(Identifier\)
rules.note: ProvidedTagBuilder has no add(Identifier); only the removed FabricTagBuilder did. Entity-type tags therefore wrap the Identifier in RegistryKey.of(RegistryKeys.ENTITY_TYPE, id), and the two registry imports are added when absent. This is the only site the old chain cannot keep, which is why it needs its own round.

rules.note: Inventory.items became private and Inventory exposes getItem(int)/getNonEquipmentItems(). rules.match: method parseOptional\(
rules.note: ItemStack.parseOptional(provider, tag) is gone; ItemStack.parse(provider, tag) returns Optional<ItemStack>, and orElse(ItemStack.EMPTY) is what parseOptional itself returned for an absent or malformed tag, so this is behaviour-preserving rather than a guess. javap 1.21.5 ItemStack shows parse(HolderLookup.Provider, Tag) -> Optional<ItemStack> and no parseOptional. Counter-example: the mod's own static FluidVariantWrapper.parseOptional(provider, tag) stays, because the find requires the ItemStack. qualifier (its own call sites in FluidTank/RenderInfo are untouched). Argument capture handles one nesting level of parens, which covers every real call site seen.

rules.match: method appendHoverText in class \w+ cannot be applied
rules.note: javap 1.21.5 Item.appendHoverText(ItemStack, Item.TooltipContext, TooltipDisplay, Consumer<Component>, TooltipFlag); the old List<Component> parameter became a consumer and TooltipDisplay is new. The find only matches a declaration (it needs the literal List<Component> in the parameter list), so the 4-argument call site in a mixin keeps its error instead of being half-rewritten; that one is a judgement call and out of scope. The body still calls .add(), which is why item-appendhovertext-consumer runs as a second round.

rules.note: Same error, same round, same file as the signature rule: the super call also gains the TooltipDisplay argument. rules.match: method add\((Mutable)?Component\)
rules.note: After the signature round the tooltip parameter is a Consumer<Component>, so tooltipComponents.add(x) must become tooltipComponents.accept(x). The first version also matched a variable named components and the build caught it: TravelersBackpackItem.addAttributeModifierTooltip takes a real List<Component> components, so those three sites became 'cannot find symbol: method accept(MutableComponent)' and the file stopped compiling. The counter-example is now excluded by name - tooltipComponents is what every tooltip consumer in this mod is called, components is what the surviving List helpers use - plus the when guard (file must already contain Consumer<Component>) and log scope.
